thesis: This episode argues that Microsoft has successfully reinvented itself as a dominant cloud and AI leader, driven by its Intelligent Cloud segment, which is now the largest and most profitable part of the company. However, it also highlights significant past failures, such as the Vista disaster and missed opportunities in consumer search and social media, which damaged its relevance as a consumer technology platform. The thesis suggests that while Microsoft's cloud advantage over competitors like AWS is strong, its historical struggles in consumer-facing areas remain a mixed factor in its overall valuation.

claims.claim: Microsoft was not serious about search until 2009, but eventually built a viable engine with small market share.
claims.quote: Search isn’t going well at Microsoft. At first it was because they just didn’t take it seriously enough. When Google first started in 1998, I think there was a lot of skepticism that the auction-based advertising business would really work.

claims.claim: Microsoft's deal to buy Yahoo fell apart, but it helped build their advertising business and cloud capabilities.
claims.quote: The deal completely falls apart. It’s interesting to try to look at the deal and figure out, even at that high price of $47 billion, was it a good deal for Microsoft? So here’s how to pull it apart.

claims.claim: Google's search business is one of the world's true marvels and a great discovery of capitalism.
claims.quote: Google is search as monetized by an ad-based auction is one of the world’s true marvels. It’s one of capitalism’s greatest discoveries.

claims.claim: Alibaba is one of the greatest investments of all time, with Microsoft holding a 40% stake.
claims.quote: Which famously is one of the greatest investments of all time. David: 40% stake of Alibaba. Ben: Collectively, those two assets together are worth over $30 billion.

claims.claim: Yahoo went away and sold for $5 billion in their most recent transaction to be co-owned by Verizon and Apollo.
claims.quote: Now, because this is counterfactual and we actually don’t know what would’ve happened, Yahoo completely went away. They sold for $5 billion in their most recent transaction to be co-owned by Verizon and Apollo.

claims.claim: Firefox was awesome, had tabs, and Google was the default search from Firefox starting around 2007.
claims.quote: And you have Firefox coming on the scene starting around 2007, where it was really making a dent, and Google was the default search from Firefox. Firefox was awesome. It had tabs.

claims.claim: Chrome wasn't a thing yet when the discussion about tabs and search was happening.
claims.quote: Ben: I don’t think Safari had tabs either. Chrome wasn’t a thing yet. I know I’m, on the one hand, talking about search, on the other hand talking about the browser, but it’s the same pot of gold.

claims.claim: Apple makes something on the order of $20 billion a year today in 2024 from Google as being the front door to Google, sending all of the iPhone search traffic to Google.
claims.quote: Well, you get to monetize it, too. The rumors are that Apple makes something on the order of $20 billion a year today in 2024 from Google as being the front door to Google, sending all of the iPhone search traffic to Google.

claims.claim: Microsoft's advertising business is now used on a number of different sites, including in partnership with Netflix, for their ad supported tier.
claims.quote: But also being, once it had all the Yahoo traffic, needed to be a scaled web service. Like a distributed computing system that operated at 24x7 uptime, with super low latency, fast response time, and huge scale. David: God, that sure sounds like the cloud.

claims.claim: Microsoft is the most valuable company in the world due to Azure, cloud, and AI.
claims.quote: And what they have done with Azure and in cloud and now with AI is, hell, they’re the most valuable company in the world.

claims.claim: The M3 MacBook Air is the finest computer the speaker has ever owned.
claims.quote: The first I mentioned earlier, M3 MacBook Air. It’s the finest computer I’ve ever owned, which I say every time I get a new Mac.

claims.claim: The M1 MacBook Pro is a beast to fly with, lightweight, fast, and beautiful.
claims.quote: I’m rocking the M1 MacBook Pro at home. It’s a 16-inch and gosh that thing is just a beast to fly with. For all the travel we’ve been doing recently, David, it has been awesome to have this incredibly lightweight, incredibly fast, just beautiful machine for flights and all sorts of travel stuff.

claims.claim: Ray Ozzie is running a new startup called Blues Wireless and was generous with time.
claims.quote: Ray is now running another startup, a new one called Blues Wireless and was just so generous to give us a couple of hours.

claims.claim: Fritz Landman is the CEO of the combined company, ClassPass and Mindbody.
claims.quote: Actually, now he is the CEO of the combined company, ClassPass and Mindbody, and talk about a person with multiple lives and careers.

claims.claim: Microsoft failed to recover as a relevant consumer technology company or an interesting platform for developers after the Vista disaster.
claims.quote: David: And I think we got to call it here, the death of Microsoft as a relevant consumer technology company. They never recovered from this as a leader.

claims.claim: Vista consumed a huge percentage of Microsoft's most talented engineers, which is company killing.
claims.quote: Ben: Money's not a scarce resource. Bad acquisitions, whatever, who cares? It's just money. But consuming a huge percentage of Microsoft's most talented engineers. That's company killing.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud segment is the largest, most profitable, and fastest-growing business in the company.
claims.quote: Intelligent Cloud today is by far the largest segment in the company by both revenue and profit, and by very, very far the fastest growing within the company. Windows is declining.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud segment generated $88 billion in revenue in fiscal 2023.
claims.quote: In fiscal 2023, Intelligent Cloud did $88 billion in revenue.

claims.claim: Microsoft's competitive advantage over AWS is its hybrid cloud capability, allowing enterprises to use both public and on-prem servers.
claims.quote: Microsoft can go to enterprises and say we are hybrid cloud. Less so today, but in the earlier days of the Azure transition saying like, hey, you need to be on on cloud? We have a world-class public cloud for you. It works great with our on-prem server offerings, and we can be hybrid for you.

claims.claim: The cloud market is so big that nothing else really mattered for Microsoft, and cloud powers everything including consumer services.
claims.quote: It turned out actually that the cloud market was so big that nothing else really mattered. All the missteps, all the losses, it makes sense. Cloud powers everything. Cloud powers tech. cloud powers all the consumer services.

claims.claim: Microsoft was lucky to own 90% of the PC market.

claims.quote: The ingredients are really starting to come together for the right talent and DNA at the company to do well in building out the cloud.

claims.claim: Microsoft failed to monetize its browser and ignored social media and developer platforms, leading to a decline in consumer relevance.
claims.quote: Microsoft built a browser, had a bunch of share, and then looked around and said, we don't really know what to do with it. I guess we'll use it for defense.
